title: MNIST DRN IBM OM HWA versus pulse-resolved program-and-verify
hypothesis: Off-chip BPTT trained against the calibrated IBM OM cap-128 endpoint distribution will reduce the KL and accuracy loss after matched pulse-resolved deployment relative to clean BPTT and a 3% per-output-channel Gaussian HWA control; explicitly retaining the published corrupt/stuck cells may leave a larger irreducible gap than the counterfactual repaired population.
motivation: This pilot tests whether HWA alone can absorb IBM OM limited bounds, stochastic programming endpoints, and published corruption before any Tiki-Taka, LoRA, or soft SET/RESET recovery is introduced. Every training arm starts by literal named-weight copy from the same seed-17, 10-epoch bounded perfect-diode DRN checkpoint at results/mnist_bounded_drn_teacher_seed17_10ep_6aa32237/20260820T140222.931115Z-809aec60-8da7bc60/checkpoints/weights.pt (SHA-256 f0036b36cebe970c5105c22ebe703d53fec99b7716215cca0e55ee09cfaf70cf). That checkpoint is the supervised bounded-DRN teacher with conductance interval [0.1020408197973068, 1], model-local amplification, four solver iterations, MNIST data seed 17, and 93.58% selected validation accuracy. The prerequisite device-model bundle must be built without refitting from the adequate adaptive conditions of the two-arm hwa_production_cap128 study ibm-reram-om-hwa-device-model-20260822-v1.

completion_criteria: The prerequisite continuous and published-corruption OM cap-128 endpoint conditions pass their predeclared held-out adequacy gates, and the immutable IBM OM HWA bundle records both source digests; otherwise this study stops before network training and does not substitute a Gaussian endpoint model.

All four training arms use the exact bounded-DRN checkpoint SHA-256 f0036b36cebe970c5105c22ebe703d53fec99b7716215cca0e55ee09cfaf70cf, identical MNIST split, topology, solver, optimizer schedule, training seed 17, and common pulse-resolved selection assignment/endpoint seed 83003.

The two IBM-aware training arms use one fixed training assignment seed 83001 and compact endpoint seed 83002; cell bounds and corrupt identity persist while endpoint randomness advances once per minibatch.
Each of the four selected checkpoints is evaluated once on each held-out full-corrupt assignment 83101 through 83104 with endpoint seeds 83201 through 83204, producing 16 matched test results.

Every pulse-resolved selection and held-out run reports programming success, SET/RESET/total pulses, verify reads, reversals, clipping, corruption, and failure, and saves an exact persistent deployment bundle linked to its source weight digest.
No on-chip-training requirement is claimed and no Tiki-Taka, LoRA, or soft SET/RESET fine-tuning is run in this pilot.
analysis_plan: Use the mean over the four held-out assignments as the primary deployment score for each training arm; report assignment-level KL, student accuracy, teacher agreement, and raw/calibrated score RMS rather than pooling examples across assignments.

Compare each IBM-aware arm against both clean and Gaussian HWA with paired assignment-level differences and retain all four points; treat this lean pilot as directional rather than a population-level significance claim.

Separate logical clean validation, common selection deployment, and held-out deployment. Never select a checkpoint from clean validation when the configured common physical selection metric is available.

Report programming success and cost beside network quality. Stratify failures into corrupt, non-corrupt budget exhaustion, bound-unreachable targets, endpoint clipping, and non-finite outcomes where recorded.
Compare repaired versus published corruption only at the corrupt sites: healthy cell identities and all non-corrupt sampled parameters are matched by construction.
Use the saved persistent deployment state, not a re-sampled endpoint, as the only eligible initialization for a later predeclared soft SET/RESET, Tiki-Taka, or LoRA recovery study.
